commits.message:
feat(resume-builder): wire Resume Variants to real create/list/duplicate

Second piece on top of the resume-persistence commit. Depends on the
companion jobFynder-BE-nestJS PR's second commit ("add resume variants
(label, variantType, parentResumeId)").

- ConsultantResumeVariantsView.tsx: took a `baseResumeId` prop (the
  currently open resume) instead of rendering a static list of 3 mock
  variant cards. Lists real variants via listResumeVariants(), creates
  via the modal below, duplicates via createResumeVariant() with a
  "Copy of X" label. Dropped the fabricated per-variant ATS/Match
  scores -- same reasoning as the ATS Check and Job Match panel calls
  earlier: no real per-variant score exists (that would need a
  quality/analyze + match call per variant, not built here), so showing
  invented numbers next to a real label/type/role would be worse than
  not showing a score at all.
- ConsultantCreateResumeVariantModal.tsx: now actually creates a
  variant instead of just showing a success toast. Removed the "Base
  From" dropdown -- it let you pick among mock variants as a base, but
  there's only one real base resume in scope here (the one currently
  open), so the field had no real options to offer. A variant of a
  variant is a real future need, just not built in this pass.
- ConsultantResumeBuilder.tsx: passes the open resume's id down as
  `baseResumeId`.

Not wired in this pass: BenchSalesCreateResumeVariantModal.tsx and
BenchSalesGenerateBlindResumeModal.tsx (the bench-sales dashboard's
variant/blind-resume actions on OTHER consultants' resumes). Checked
before starting -- CORE's /resume routes are ownership-scoped to
`req.user._id` by design, so a bench-sales user cannot create/read/
write a resume owned by a different consultant with the current auth
model. Wiring those two screens for real would mean either bypassing
that check (a real security bug) or building a proper delegated-access
model first (an org/assignment-based permission layer -- there's a
ConsultantAssignment table in the schema that looks like the right
foundation for it, not yet explored). Flagging rather than building
around the gap.

Verified locally: `tsc --noEmit` clean. Browser pass against the mock
server (extended with in-memory /resume/:id/variants handlers) --
created a variant with a real label/type/target-role, confirmed it
rendered correctly, then duplicated it and confirmed a second real
variant appeared with the correct "Copy of ..." label. Not verified
against the live database -- same blocker as the first commit.
